name: worker-sandbox

plan-approved.quote: decline review round 5 and approve plan

summary: Build worker-sandbox as designed in docs/designs/worker-sandbox.md (locked at 6ca02a1): every delegate agent run starts inside a Windows AppContainer on a reserved slot drive letter, with per-run grants, a slot ledger and a patched copy of Cursor's node.exe. READING THE BRIEFS: 'file N' means entry N under the design's 'Detailed Implementation Plan > Target Files to Create/Modify'; the design is the source of truth wherever a brief is shorter. Profiles (code, code-hard) pick the delegate worker model from skills/delegate/models.json. WORKER TASKS: eleven, in five phases, following the design's Build order with one deliberate change: phase 2 runs after phase 1 instead of beside it, because every task's test command is scripts/test.ps1, which phase 1 creates. Phase 3's five task files are the G7 experiment, taken as one group: each is written in two parts (Decided / Yours to decide), and the group is afterwards compared with fb-stages, the earlier tightly specified code-hard task (the feature skill's build step 4, D19 in docs/test-plan.md). Phase 4's two tasks run one after the other, because both test runs execute the container tests, which reserve real drive letters and slot profiles. LEAD AND USER STEPS (not tasks): (1) before phase 1, with the user's approval, the lead creates the frozen copy (git worktree add --detach D:/cross-agent-loop.frozen 6ca02a1; moved on 2026-11-14 to main's 8cb3a3a and then 30d2d29, which add only the task size gate) and points ~/.claude/skills/delegate and ~/.claude/skills/feature at it (G6); (2) the first sandboxed run on the real machine needs the user to approve three drive letters (CUJ 1); tests reserve and release their own; (3) after phase 5 the lead runs the checks that need a real Cursor login or a human (the Live canary as worker, lens and council seat; the suite inside the sandbox; the delegate regression; crash recovery; overhead; the token-refresh check over at least a day) and records them, the G6 skillDir check and the G7 comparison in docs/test-plan.md and docs/HANDOFF.md. No step involves secrets, credentials or deploys. TASK SIZE AND TIMEOUTS (re-planned 2026-11-14 after sandbox-core's 50-minute timeout; docs/test-plan.md): each unmerged task targets about 20 worker minutes or 600 lines, checked by the comprehension preflight's size gate (skills/delegate/personas/task-size-standard.md), and its test command runs only its own tests (skills/delegate/tests, or a Pester filter on one Describe), so workers no longer run the full suite. Workers launch with delegate.ps1 -TimeoutSec 2700 and verify with feature.ps1 verify -TimeoutSec 900. The phase tests run the fast suite (phases 2 and 3) or the full suite (phases 1, 4 and 5); the full suite took 695 s on 2026-11-12 and grows with the container tests, so the lead runs phase tests with a timeout of at least 1800 s.

phases.rationale: Groundwork with no sandbox code: one test command for workers and the lead, and no taskkill.exe anywhere, so this repo's own suite can later run inside the sandbox.

tasks.title: scripts/test.ps1: the repo's one test command
tasks.brief: Create scripts/test.ps1 as the design's file 7 specifies: param([switch]$Fast); Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.5; New-PesterConfiguration with Run.Path set to whichever of skills/feature/tests and skills/delegate/tests exist (resolved from the script's own folder, so it works from any working folder; if neither exists, print 'no test folders' and exit 0), Run.PassThru = $true, TestRegistry.Enabled = $false (Pester's test registry writes HKCU, which an AppContainer cannot write), Filter.ExcludeTag 'Live' plus 'Slow' with -Fast, Output.Verbosity 'Normal'; exit with [Math]::Min($result.FailedCount, 250). Nothing else changes. Its contract is tested by kill-tree.

tasks.title: Replace taskkill.exe with a .NET tree kill
tasks.brief: Add Stop-ProcessTree -ProcessId to feature.ps1 ([Diagnostics.Process]::GetProcessById($id).Kill($true), ignore 'process has exited' and 'not found', wait up to 10 s) and use it at the three taskkill.exe sites: the reconcile orphan kill (~line 1806), the verify timeout in Invoke-TaskTestCommand (~2290) and the Invoke-DoctorCommand timeout (~2556). In delegate.ps1, replace the timeout's '& taskkill.exe /T /F /PID' (line ~349) with 'try { $proc.Kill($true) } catch {}; $proc.WaitForExit(10000) | Out-Null'; nothing else in delegate.ps1 changes in this task. Add an UNTAGGED feature.Tests.ps1 test (not Slow) that a two-level child process tree (pwsh starting pwsh starting Start-Sleep) is fully gone after Stop-ProcessTree. Acceptance also includes: 'git grep -n taskkill -- skills/feature/scripts skills/delegate/scripts' finds nothing. The test command runs the full suite because the existing tests that cover these kill sites (feature.Tests.ps1 lines ~1485 and ~2281) are tagged Slow. The new test gets Stop-ProcessTree through the file's existing pattern, BeforeAll { . (Get-FeatureFunctionScript -Name @('Stop-ProcessTree')) } (see TestHelpers.ps1 and feature.Tests.ps1 ~140), never by dot-sourcing the whole script. Also add an untagged Describe 'scripts/test.ps1' in feature.Tests.ps1 that builds a temp folder with one passing, one failing and one Slow-tagged test, runs the script's configuration logic against it with -Fast, and asserts the Slow test was excluded and the exit code is 1; and that a run with no test folders prints 'no test folders' and exits 0 (point the script at the temp folder through a parameter or environment variable the script reads; if test-runner gave it none, add -Path to scripts/test.ps1, which this task may edit).

phases.rationale: The sandbox core: the native launcher and everything that does not depend on a run: support check, runtime cache and node.exe patch, reserved letters. Fully specified by the design (files 1 and 2, the functions the Build order lists for phase 2).

tasks.title: SandboxNative.cs and Sandbox.psm1 part 1 (support, runtime cache and patch, letters)
tasks.brief: Implement exactly what docs/designs/worker-sandbox.md specifies for phase 2. File 1, SandboxNative.cs: XagentSandbox with EnsureProfile, DeleteProfile, Start, Wait, Kill, Finish, IsAppContainer, and RunHandle, with the constants, handle-inheritance and environment-block rules given there. File 2, Sandbox.psm1: its Settings, Test-LetterFree, Test-SandboxSupport (all checks except the read-list rule, which phase 3 adds), Get-SandboxRuntime (version choice, reuse contract, copy, patch, prune), Get-SandboxConfig, Set-SandboxLetters and Initialize-SandboxLetters, with the exact error strings; every thrown error starts with 'sandbox:'. Pinned here because other tasks consume them: (a) Test-SandboxSupport returns {ok, build, cursorVersion, uv, patternCount, letters, problems[]} where letters is {reserved: bool, runtime: <letter or null>, slots: [<letters>], states: {<letter>: 'free'|'ours'|'used'}}; no letters reserved is NOT a problem (ok stays true, reserved = false); (b) the copy path first deletes any existing <version> folder and any <version>.partial; (c) the module loads SandboxNative.cs only if the type is not loaded yet (if (-not ('XagentSandbox' -as [type])) { Add-Type -Path ... }), so importing it twice in one process works. Tests: the phase-2 unit tests listed in file 5, in skills/delegate/tests/Sandbox.Tests.ps1, using XAGENT_SANDBOX_ROOT and XAGENT_CURSOR_ROOT under TestDrive; no test calls a real model or touches the user's sandbox.json. The version-choice test takes its oracle from the real launcher: it extracts Parse-VersionString from %LOCALAPPDATA%/cursor-agent/cursor-agent.ps1 with the PowerShell AST, and skips with a reason when that file is unreadable. Reference: docs/designs/worker-sandbox-probe/ (probe5.ps1's AC class; the pattern bytes and offset in the README). Test-LetterFree stays private (not exported); test it with InModuleScope. (d) For a Cursor version whose node.exe has the pattern a number of times other than 1 and libuv below 1.53, Test-SandboxSupport's problem string is exactly 'Cursor <version>: node.exe pipe-name pattern found <n> times; Sandbox.psm1 needs an update (use -NoSandbox to run unsandboxed)', the same text Get-SandboxRuntime throws after its 'sandbox: ' prefix; delegate.ps1 joins problems with '; ' after 'sandbox: '. TEST REPOS: the sandbox refuses any repo or worktree under %USERPROFILE%, and Pester's TestDrive is under it. So every test that needs a sandboxed repo or worktree creates it under a test root on the drive of the repo being tested, outside the worktree: $testRoot = Join-Path (Split-Path <repo root> -Qualifier) ('xagent-tests-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0,8)), created in BeforeAll and removed in an AfterAll finally. If that drive's root is not writable, or the repo is under %USERPROFILE%, those Describes skip with a reason. Only XAGENT_SANDBOX_ROOT, XAGENT_CURSOR_ROOT and XAGENT_LOG_DIR stay in TestDrive, and -NoSandbox cases may use TestDrive repos.

phases.rationale: Running one sandboxed task: read list, environment, grants, ledger, slots, run home, launch, stop, canary and release. Split on 2026-11-14 into five sequential code-hard tasks of about 20 worker minutes each, after sandbox-core's 50-minute timeout (docs/test-plan.md) and plan review 3 (sandbox-access then split in two by its preflight size gate): the read list and environment, then the grant list and ledger, then slots and release, then the run lifecycle, then the canary with the isolation and read-list runs and the probes. Each task's test runs only skills/delegate/tests; the phase test runs the fast suite. The five task files are the G7 group.

tasks.title: Sandbox.psm1 part 2b: slots, release, crash recovery
tasks.brief: Phase 3, task 3 of 5. Implement Get-SandboxSlot -TimeoutSec and Remove-SandboxLetters. Get-SandboxSlot releases and disposes every mutex it rejects before trying the next slot, on the live-ledger and abandoned-mutex paths alike; only Stop-SandboxRun (next task) releases a taken slot's mutex. On a free slot with a dead run's ledger it calls Remove-SandboxGrants. Remove-SandboxLetters parses CheckNetIsolation LoopbackExempt -s for exemptions still registered for the two SIDs and returns each with its -d command. Tests: a unit test of that parse on a captured text fixture in skills/delegate/tests/fixtures/. Container tests are tagged Sandbox and follow file 5's skip rules (IsAppContainer() true, build below 26300, or fewer than three free letters); BeforeAll reserves the three highest free letters with Set-SandboxLetters and AfterAll calls Remove-SandboxLetters in a finally. Container tests: reserve and release (three mappings and two profiles, all removed, with <Root>\sandbox and the letters in sandbox.json); release refused while a slot is held; with both slot mutexes held, a third Get-SandboxSlot fails with the no-free-slot error after -TimeoutSec 4; crash recovery: a child process takes a slot mutex and exits without releasing it, leaving a ledger with grants on a test folder, and the next Get-SandboxSlot takes that slot and removes those grants (assert with icacls that the SID is gone); a ledger naming a live process makes the slot busy. G7 two-part task. Decided: mutex names, the slot result {letter, mutex, container, sid}, every error string, and the public function signatures as the design states them. Yours to decide: internal helpers, internal tests beyond the listed ones, and the order of work. The design (file 2's phase-3 functions and file 5's tests) is the source of truth. SandboxNative.cs may change only if a test proves it must. Tests go in skills/delegate/tests/Sandbox.Tests.ps1 beside phase 2's; keep its BeforeAll/AfterAll environment handling. Each task is sized to about 20 worker minutes; the earlier tasks' helpers are in the code, so call them rather than adding a second version. TEST REPOS: the sandbox refuses any repo or worktree under %USERPROFILE%, and Pester's TestDrive is under it. So every test that needs a sandboxed repo or worktree creates it under a test root on the drive of the repo being tested, outside the worktree: $testRoot = Join-Path (Split-Path <repo root> -Qualifier) ('xagent-tests-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0,8)), created in BeforeAll and removed in an AfterAll finally.
